strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Interleaved Scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all_reduce operations with local scale/unscale operations between each stage, mirroring the reference implementation. 8 collective dispatches with full W*S payload each. Straightforward but highest latency due to sequential dependencies and no fusion opportunities.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-AllReduce Pipeline Batching
strategies.desc: Pre-compute all scale factors and buffer transformations, then batch multiple all_reduce calls with overlapping computation where possible by preparing the next stage's buffer during current all_reduce. Still 8 dispatches but hides local compute (scaling loops) in communication time through careful staging of buffer preparation.

strategies.name: Vectorized Per-Shard Scaling Operations
strategies.desc: Replace element-wise loops over W shards with vectorized tensor operations using view/reshape and broadcast multiplication, enabling hardware acceleration of local scaling. 8 all_reduce dispatches remain, but local compute cost reduced by ~10-100x through eliminating Python loops and leveraging tensor parallelism.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + All-Gather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Decompose each all_reduce into reduce_scatter followed by all_gather, allowing per-rank local scaling to happen on smaller S-sized chunks between the two primitives. 16 total dispatches (8 stages × 2 primitives) but each operates on smaller payloads (W*S for AG, S average for RS), potentially better bandwidth utilization.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Tree
strategies.desc:
Exploit potential multi-node structure (world_size=224 suggests multiple nodes) by performing intra-node reductions first, then inter-node reductions with scaling applied at node boundaries. Reduces cross-node traffic by factor of cores_per_node while maintaining correctness; total dispatches depend on topology but typically 8-16 with asymmetric payload sizes.
